questions.q: Identify the colour of compound 'X' in the sequence of the reaction.
questions.explain: Colour comes from extended conjugation, which absorbs visible light. Phenolphthalein is the compound made from phthalic anhydride and phenol. In mild base the ring opens into the quinoid form, a long conjugated system, which is pink. With excess NaOH, OH- adds to the central carbon, which becomes sp3 and breaks the conjugation. The product X then absorbs no visible light, so it is colourless.

questions.q: Consider the following reaction sequence. Compound (y) develops characteristic colour with neutral FeCl3 solution. Identify the INCORRECT statement.
options: y dissolves in NaHCO3 and evolves a gas
Both x and y dissolve in NaOH
Both x and y burn with sooty flame
x is more acidic than y
questions.explain: First find x. Vapour density 47 means molar mass 94. From 76.6% C, carbon is about 72, which is 6 C atoms. 6.38% H gives 6 H, and what is left (16) is one O. So x is C6H5OH, phenol. CO2, NaOH, 120°C and pressure is the Kolbe reaction, which gives salicylic acid (y). Now check each statement. A is true: COOH is a stronger acid than carbonic acid, so y gives CO2 with NaHCO3. B is true: both are acidic enough for NaOH. C is true: aromatic compounds burn with a sooty flame. D is false: salicylic acid is the more acidic one, not phenol. So D is the incorrect statement.

questions.q: Phenol reacts with Na to give the main product and gas x; benzoic acid reacts with NaHCO3 to give the main product and gas y. Find molar mass(x) + molar mass(y).
questions.explain: Work out the gas in each reaction. Phenol has an acidic O-H, and Na reacts with it to give sodium phenoxide and H2, so x is H2 (molar mass 2). Benzoic acid is stronger than carbonic acid, so with NaHCO3 it gives sodium benzoate, water and CO2. So y is CO2 (molar mass 44). The sum is 2 + 44 = 46.

questions.q: The total number of aromatic compounds/species from the following is:
questions.explain: Aromatic means cyclic, planar, fully conjugated and 4n+2 pi electrons (Huckel). Go through them. p-Benzoquinone has C=O groups in the ring, so it is not a fully conjugated ring of p-orbitals and is not aromatic. Tropylium has 7 sp2 carbons with 6 pi electrons, so it is aromatic. Phenanthrene is aromatic. Dihydronaphthalene keeps a full benzene ring, so it is counted. The cyclobutadiene dication has 2 pi electrons, so it is aromatic. The cyclohexadienyl anion has an sp3 carbon that breaks the cycle, so it is not. Total: 4.

questions.q: Designate whether each of the following compounds is aromatic or not aromatic.
questions.explain: Test each ring with Huckel's rule: cyclic, planar, fully conjugated, and 4n+2 pi electrons. (a) cyclopentadienyl anion has 6, aromatic. (b) cyclopentadienyl cation has 4, not aromatic. (c) cyclobutadiene dication has 2, aromatic. (d) cyclobutadiene dianion has 6, aromatic. (e) tropylium cation has 6, aromatic. (f) cyclooctatetraene has 8 and is not planar, so not aromatic. (g) cyclobutadiene has 4, not aromatic. (h) cyclopropenyl cation has 2, aromatic. So a, c, d, e, h are aromatic.

questions.q: Which of the following are aromatic?
questions.explain: Check each one. B is a benzene ring with a vinyl side chain. The ring is a complete aromatic ring, so B is aromatic. D is [14]annulene, with 14 pi electrons, which fits 4n+2 (n = 3) and can stay planar, so it is aromatic. A has an sp3 CH2 in the second ring, so it is not conjugated all the way round. C is [10]annulene, which fits 4n+2 on paper, but the hydrogens inside the ring crowd each other and force it out of plane, so it is not aromatic. So B and D.

questions.q: Which of the following molecule/species is most stable?
questions.explain: Aromatic stabilisation makes a species more stable, so look for the aromatic one. A, the cyclopropenyl cation, is cyclic, planar and fully conjugated with 2 pi electrons (4n+2, n = 0), so it is aromatic and extra stable. B, the cyclopentadienyl cation, has 4 pi electrons, so it is antiaromatic and unstable. C, the cyclopropenyl system with two extra electrons, has 4 pi electrons, so it is antiaromatic as well. D is a plain cyclohexadiene with no aromatic bonus. So A is the most stable.

questions.q: Compound from the following that will not produce precipitate on reaction with AgNO3 is:
questions.explain: A precipitate with AgNO3 means the C-Br bond ionises to give Br-, which forms AgBr. That needs a reasonably stable carbocation. A gives the cyclopropenyl cation, which is aromatic and very stable. B gives the benzyl cation, stabilised by resonance with the ring. C gives an allyl-type cation, also resonance stabilised. In D, Br sits on a C=C carbon (vinylic). Its lone pair delocalises into the double bond, so the C-Br bond is stronger, and a vinyl cation is unstable. So D does not ionise and gives no precipitate.

questions.q: Correct statements for the given reaction are: squaric acid A + 2 eq OH- -> B. A: B is aromatic. B: completion of reaction is very slow. C: A shows tautomerism. D: C-C bond lengths in B are same.
questions.explain: Take the statements one by one. Squaric acid loses two H+ with 2 OH-. The resulting dianion B has the 4-membered ring with 2 pi electrons delocalised over it, which fits 4n+2 (n = 0), so B is aromatic (A is true). In an aromatic ring all the C-C bonds are equal, so D is true. Acid-base proton transfers are very fast, so B (the reaction is very slow) is false. A shows tautomerism between its C=O and OH forms, so C is true. So A, C and D.
